# Small mass outside an arbitrary complete parity core

Historical claim of scope (pending review here): proved, using the previously proved ordinary simplex-rigidity theorem. For every \(d\ge2\) there is a number \(\rho_d>0\), independent of the number of integer coordinates, with the following property.

Let \(n\ge1\), let \(\mathcal C\subset\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d\) be a convex body, and write \(K_z=\{x:(z,x)\in\mathcal C\}\). Suppose a set \(P_0\subset\mathbb Z^n\) contains exactly one representative of each parity class, and every \(K_w\), \(w\in P_0\), has positive \(d\)-volume. Put

\[
 L=2^n,\qquad V_w=|K_w|,\qquad m=\min_{w\in P_0}V_w,
 \qquad E=\sum_{z\notin P_0}|K_z|.
\]

If \(E\le\rho_dm\), the mixed source has an actual point with every containing closed halfspace of mass at least

\[
                 \frac{\Gamma_d}{L}
                    \left(\sum_{w\in P_0}V_w+E\right).       \tag{1}
\]

No convex-position, empty-polytope, congruence, or common-shape condition is imposed on the core. No bounded coordinate range for its vertices is required. The smallness condition is a restriction on the source and is not proved for arbitrary bodies. In particular this theorem is not a solution of unrestricted OC.

Throughout, lower-dimensional integer fibers contribute zero \(d\)-volume. The proof explicitly allows their presence. The argument below uses the strict inequality \(\Gamma_d<1/2\), and makes no assertion of a positive constant by this argument when \(d=1\).

## 1. Ordinary inputs and uniform compactness

Write \(\Gamma=\Gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d\). We use the proved result in `candidate e2c55c91458e1e8c`: the maximum ordinary normalized depth \(D(B)\) of a \(d\)-body satisfies

\[
 D(B)\ge\Gamma,\qquad D(B)=\Gamma\iff B\text{ is a simplex}. \tag{2}
\]

We also use its continuity under Hausdorff convergence to a full-dimensional convex body. The remaining ordinary input is classical Grünbaum at the true centroid, including its simplex equality directions. These inputs do not involve a mixed-integer assertion.

The following uniform compactness facts will be useful. Normalize a maximum-volume inscribed simplex of \(B\) to

\[
 T=\operatorname{conv}(0,e_1,\ldots,e_d),\quad v=1/d!,
 \quad g=g_T.
\]

Replacing one simplex vertex shows that all barycentric coordinates of every point of \(B\) have absolute value at most one. Consequently

\[
                T\subset B\subset[-1,1]^d.                \tag{3}
\]

As \(D(B)\downarrow\Gamma\), every such normalized \(B\) converges uniformly to \(T\) in Hausdorff distance. Indeed any sequence violating this has a Hausdorff-convergent subsequence by \(3\). Its limit has depth \(\Gamma\), hence is a simplex by \(2\). The maximum inscribed-simplex volume remains \(v\): approximation of the limiting vertices gives the upper bound, and \(T\subset B\) gives the lower bound. The limiting simplex therefore equals \(T\).

Here is a uniform companion fact. Suppose

\[
 (A+C)/2\subset B,\qquad
 D(B),D(C)\le\Gamma(1+\theta),\qquad
 (1+\theta)^{-1}\le |C|/|B|\le1+\theta.                    \tag{4}
\]

After \(3\), choose \(p_0\in A\) and replace only this pair by

\[
                A'=A-p_0,\qquad C'=C+p_0.                \tag{5}
\]

Then \(0\in A'\), \(C'\subset2B\), and \(A'\subset2(B-B)\). In particular all the translated bodies lie in the ball of radius \(R=4\sqrt d\). Opposite translations preserve \(4\), all volumes and ordinary depths. As \(\theta\downarrow0\), \(B\to T\), \(|B|,|C'|\to v\), and \(C'\) approaches the compact class of simplices in \(2[-1,1]^d\) with volume \(v\). Otherwise a contradicting bounded sequence has a full-dimensional limit with depth \(\Gamma\), and \(2\) applies.

In particular the ratio of the maximum inscribed-simplex volume of \(C'\) to \(|B|\) tends uniformly to one. The maximum-inscribed-simplex functional is Hausdorff continuous here, by compactness of its vertex tuples and approximation of limiting vertices. These statements are uniform over *all pairs* satisfying \(4\); they do not require fixing the number of pairs first.

## 2. A uniform local repair for a finite star of pairs

Put

\[
 N=d+1,\quad b=1/N,\quad J=\lceil N/2\rceil,\quad
 \kappa=J/N-\Gamma>0,\quad
 \eta=\kappa/2,\quad \alpha=J/N-\eta=\Gamma+\kappa/2.       \tag{6}
\]

There is \(\theta_d>0\) with the following local property, for an arbitrary finite number of pairs. Suppose all \(A_j,B,C_j\) are \(d\)-bodies and

\[
 \frac{A_j+C_j}{2}\subset B,\quad
 D(B),D(C_j)\le\Gamma(1+\theta_d),\quad
 \frac1{1+\theta_d}\le\frac{|C_j|}{|B|}\le1+\theta_d,
 \quad 0< e:=\sum_j|A_j|\le\theta_d|B|.                  \tag{7}
\]

Then a point \(y\in\operatorname{int}B\) satisfies, for every nonconstant affine functional \(f\) and every list of real numbers \(\beta_j\),

\[
 |B\cap\{f\ge f(y)\}|+
 \sum_j\bigl(|A_j\cap\{f\ge f(y)+\beta_j\}|
            +|C_j\cap\{f\ge f(y)-\beta_j\}|\bigr)
                  \ge\Gamma|B|+\alpha e.                 \tag{8}
\]

The pair copies in this lemma are separate sources. Its eventual use will verify that no actual fiber is counted twice.

We give the uniform proof, in particular the dependence of approximation errors on \(e\). Normalize \(B\) as in \(3\), and make the pair translations \(5\) separately for each \(j\). Equation \(8\) is invariant under these translations: they add opposite constants to the two thresholds and thus only change the arbitrary \(\beta_j\). This is a calculation for each pair, not an assertion that all pair translations are one ambient shear.

Let \(\lambda_i\), \(0\le i\le d\), be the barycentric functions of \(T\), with \(n_i=\nabla\lambda_i\). Set \(q=N-J+1\) and

\[
 \delta_0=N^{-N/(2q)}-1/N>0,\qquad \delta=\delta_0/2.    \tag{9}
\]

The positivity follows from \(q>N/2\). For sufficiently small \(\theta_d\), uniformly in \(j\), choose a simplex \(S_j\subset C_j'\) whose volume ratio to an outer homothetic copy \(T^+\supset B\), with \(T^+\to T\), is at least

\[
       \left(\frac{b+\delta}{b+\delta_0}\right)^q<1.       \tag{10}
\]

Section 1 justifies this uniformly. For every \(p\in A_j'\), the simplex \((p+S_j)/2\subset T^+\) has a nonnegative column-stochastic barycentric matrix. The centered-row determinant estimate in `candidate 986ab1688d049a3b` reads, for decreasing row maxima \(r_1\ge\cdots\ge r_N\),

\[
 |\det P|\le N^{N/2}2^{-d}\prod_{i=2}^N r_i
              \le N^{N/2}2^{-d}r_J^q.                   \tag{11}
\]

Its determinant is \(2^{-d}|S_j|/|T^+|\); \(10\) gives \(r_J\ge b+\delta\). Writing the barycentric functions of the outer copy as \(b+(\lambda_i-b)/(1+t)\), \(t\ge0\), yields at least \(J\) indices with

\[
              \lambda_i(p)+h_{C_j'}(\lambda_i)
                               \ge2b+2\delta.            \tag{12}
\]

Define fixed measurable subsets and their credits before choosing \(y\):

\[
 A_{j,i}'=\{p\in A_j':\lambda_i(p)+h_{C_j'}(\lambda_i)
                                    \ge2b+\delta\},
 \qquad c_{j,i}=|A_{j,i}'|,\quad c_i=\sum_jc_{j,i},
 \quad\bar c=N^{-1}\sum_ic_i.
\]

All masses here are in the common normalized frame. Pointwise multiplicity in \(12\), followed by integration, gives

\[
              0\le c_i\le e,\qquad \bar c\ge Je/N.       \tag{13}
\]

The fixed credits remain valid under uniform perturbations. For \(f_i=\lambda_i+a\cdot x\), \(|a|\le\varepsilon\), and \(y\in B\) with \(\max_i(\lambda_i(y)-b)_+\le\sigma\), put \(r_j=(|A_j|/|C_j|)^{1/d}\). A homothetic \(C_j'\)-cap of mass \(|A_j|\) proves, for every tilt,

\[
 |A_j'\cap\{f_i\ge f_i(y)+\beta\}|+
 |C_j'\cap\{f_i\ge f_i(y)-\beta\}|
 \ge |A_j'\cap\{f_i\ge2f_i(y)-h_{C_j'}(f_i)
                                      +\operatorname{width}_{C_j'}(f_i)r_j\}|.
                                                               \tag{14}
\]

For all sufficiently small \(\theta_d\), the width in direction \(\lambda_i\) is at most three. The bounded translated frame then shows that every \(p\in A_{j,i}'\) exceeds the threshold on the right of \(14\) by at least

\[
                      \delta-2\sigma-3r_j-6R\varepsilon. \tag{15}
\]

Choose \(\varepsilon\le\delta/(24R)\) and ensure \(\sigma\le\delta/8\) and \(r_j\le\delta/12\). The margin is at least \(\delta/4>0\). Thus the two actual endpoint caps pay \(c_{j,i}\), uniformly for every tilt and the same fixed nearby directions and centers. Since \(r_j^d\le\theta_d(1+\theta_d)\), one smallness condition controls all \(j\).

Now let \(g_B\) be the TRUE ordinary centroid of \(B\), and define a displacement \(v_B\) by

\[
 n_i\cdot v_B=\frac{c_i-\bar c}{N\Gamma|B|},\qquad
 y=g_B+v_B.                                               \tag{16}
\]

The right sides sum to zero; the barycentric gradients have precisely this dependence, so the displacement exists. In standard coordinates

\[
             |v_B|\le K_d e/|B|,\qquad
                  K_d=\frac{\sqrt d}{N\Gamma}.           \tag{17}
\]

At the proper centroid section of \(T\), the coarea density for \(lambda_i\) is \(N\Gamma v\). Hausdorff convergence of convex bodies and proper sections, uniformly on a compact set of nearby planes, implies the following. Given \(\zeta>0\), first decrease the fixed \(\varepsilon>0\) and choose a fixed \(h>0\); then decrease \(\theta_d\), so that

\[
 \left|S_B(f_i,f_i(g_B)+t)-N\Gamma|B|\right|
       \le\zeta|B|\qquad(|a|\le\varepsilon, |t|\le h).   \tag{18}
\]

Here \(S_B\) is section \((d-1)\)-volume divided by the norm of the functional's gradient. The elementary proper-section continuity proof is recorded in Section 5 of `candidate 1350a6f7ed8eb7d0`: approximate section points by interior section points before moving the plane. No facet smoothness is assumed. All these planes are proper.

Choose the fixed constants so that

\[
 \zeta K_d(\sqrt d+1)\le\eta/2,\qquad
 \varepsilon\le\min\{1,\delta/(24R),\eta/(2\sqrt d)\}.
                                                               \tag{19}
\]

Then decrease \(\theta_d\) again so that \(16\) gives \(y\in\operatorname{int}T\), \(\sigma\le\delta/8\), and \(|f_i(y)-f_i(g_B)|\le h\). These follow uniformly from \(g_B\to g\) and \(17\). The signed coarea integral from \(g_B\) to \(y\), \(18\), and \(19\) give

\[
 |B\cap\{f_i\ge f_i(y)\}|
             \ge\Gamma|B|-(c_i-\bar c)-\eta e.           \tag{20}
\]

The initial bound at \(g_B\) is exact ordinary Grünbaum. More explicitly, the error in replacing the coarea integral by \(N\Gamma|B|n_i\cdot v_B\) is at most

\[
 \zeta|B|\,|(n_i+a)\cdot v_B|
          +N\Gamma|B|\,|a\cdot v_B|\le\eta e.
\]

Thus there is no additive Hausdorff error independent of \(e\). Combining \(20\) with the sum of \(14\) proves \(8\) for all the oriented facet neighborhoods, by \(13\).

For the remaining unit normals, the centroid caps of the fixed simplex have a positive uniform gap \(G\) over \(\Gamma\), on the compact complement of these neighborhoods. This follows from the exact simplex equality directions. Uniform cap-volume continuity for \(B\to T\), \(y\to g\), gives at least \((\Gamma+G/2)|B|\) in \(B\) alone. Decrease \(\theta_d\) so that \(\alpha e\le G|B|/2\). This proves \(8\) in every remaining direction. If an associated ambient cap has zero continuous normal, its whole middle fiber contributes \(|B|\); decrease \(\theta_d\) also so that \(\Gamma+\alpha\theta_d<1\).

All choices in this proof depend only on \(d\). The number of pairs never enters: the compactness assertions are uniform over the class \(4\), and the only accumulated approximation error is \(eta\sum_j|A_j|\). This completes the local lemma.

## 3. Exact parity grouping, including null outer fibers

Suppose \(E<2^{-d}m\). If a nonempty outer fiber is at \(p\notin P_0\), let \(v(p)\in P_0\) be the unique point with the same parity, and put \(w(p)=(p+v(p))/2\in\mathbb Z^n\). Any \(x\in K_p\) gives

\[
                   (x+K_{v(p)})/2\subset K_{w(p)}.
\]

The right fiber has volume at least \(2^{-d}m\). It therefore belongs to the core, even when the original \(K_p\) had zero volume. Thus every nonempty outer base has the form

\[
                 p=2w-v,\qquad w,v\in P_0,\quad w\ne v. \tag{21}
\]

There are finitely many such bases, independently of how large the core coordinates are. Within a fixed target \(w\), different outer bases have distinct partners \(v=2w-p\). In fact the pairs are globally unique: equality \(2w-v=2w'-v'\) first implies \(v\equiv v'\pmod2\), hence \(v=v'\) by the transversal property and then \(w=w'\).

Group the positive-volume outer fibers by their target and write

\[
 E_w=\sum_{p:w(p)=w}|K_p|,\qquad \sum_w E_w=E.           \tag{22}
\]

The associated pairs use neither \(K_w\) nor any other core fiber twice within that group. For a cap through \((w,y)\), the continuous thresholds at \(p\) and \(v(p)\) sum to twice its threshold at \(w\), because \(p+v(p)=2w\). They are exactly the arbitrary paired thresholds in \(8\), with whatever values the single actual integer tilt supplies.

## 4. Failure implies the hypotheses of every local repair

Choose

\[
                     0<\rho_d\le\min\{2^{-d-1},\theta_d\}.
                                                               \tag{23}
\]

If \(E=0\), choose a largest core fiber and its ordinary centroid. Its own-fiber Grünbaum bound proves \(1\). Suppose \(E>0\) and, for contradiction, no actual point attains \(1\). Set \(\bar V=L^{-1}\sum_wV_w\) and \(T_*=(\Gamma/L)(\sum_wV_w+E)\). Every point in a core fiber has mixed depth at least its ordinary absolute depth in that fiber. Therefore failure implies, for every \(w\),

\[
       \Gamma V_w\le D(K_w)V_w<T_*
                         =\Gamma(\bar V+E/L).           \tag{24}
\]

Taking a smallest core volume \(m\) and summing the upper bounds on the other \(L-1\) volumes gives

\[
 \bar V<m+(L-1)E/L,\qquad
 \max_wV_w<m+E,\qquad
 D(K_w)<\Gamma(1+E/m).                                 \tag{25}
\]

Consequently, for every core pair,

\[
 \frac1{1+\rho_d}\le V_v/V_w\le1+\rho_d,
 \qquad E_w/V_w\le\rho_d,
 \qquad D(K_w),D(K_v)\le\Gamma(1+\rho_d).                \tag{26}
\]

These are uniform in \(L=2^n\). Every positive target group thus satisfies the local lemma \(7\). At its repaired point \(y_w\in K_w\), every actual containing cap has mass at least

\[
                             \Gamma V_w+\alpha E_w.     \tag{27}
\]

This uses the disjoint actual fibers checked in Section 3; the contributions of all unused fibers are nonnegative. Purely integer caps contain the whole target fiber and were included in the local lemma. For \(E_w=0\), use the ordinary centroid, giving \(27\) with its second term zero.

Finally the mean of the \(L\) lower bounds \(27\) is

\[
 \frac{\Gamma\sum_wV_w+\alpha E}{L}
       >\frac{\Gamma(\sum_wV_w+E)}L=T_*,                \tag{28}
\]

since \(\alpha>\Gamma\) and \(E>0\). At least one of the actual constructed core points therefore exceeds the supposedly unattainable target. This contradiction proves the theorem.

All estimates were proved for boundary-through-point caps. A general containing closed halfspace contains its parallel through-point halfspace. Nonvertical boundaries have zero \(d\)-volume on every positive-volume fiber; vertical caps retain the whole target fiber and no boundary mass is discarded. Zero-volume fibers play a role only in the exact grouping argument, never as an extra positive source charge.

## 5. Scope of the constant and the reduction

The existence of (
ho_d>0) is nonconstructive only through ordinary compactness and simplex rigidity. It is independent of \(n\), of the positions of the parity representatives, of the shapes or relative locations of the core fibers, and of the number of positive outer pairs. The local normalizations are analysis of separate candidate points; pair translations are threshold identities, not unauthorized independent alterations of the actual body.

The proof does not require the Hausdorff distance to a simplex to be \(o(E)\), nor \(o(E_w)\). Exact Grünbaum at each true core centroid supplies the baseline, while section-density approximation is multiplied by the chosen displacement \(O(E_w/V_w)\). This distinction is essential when one target group carries a much smaller mass than the total outside mass.

It remains a restricted regime theorem: a complete parity transversal carrying all but a sufficiently small mass is an explicit hypothesis, not a conclusion about every mixed convex source. No intrinsic extension beyond the full \(d\)-volume setting is claimed here.

# Small mass outside an arbitrary complete parity core

**OC near a complete parity core with dimension-only mass threshold**

For every d>=2 there is rho_d>0 such that the following holds for all n>=1. In an actual mixed-integer convex source choose a core of exactly one positive d-dimensional fiber from each of the 2^n parity classes. If the total d-volume E in all other fibers is at most rho_d times the smallest core-fiber volume, then some point of the source has normalized halfspace depth at least 2^(-n)(d/(d+1))^d. The small-outside-mass hypothesis is essential to the scope of this statement.

Scope limits: The small-outside-mass condition is substantive and is not established for arbitrary sources. Uses ordinary simplex equality rigidity and a uniform local star repair from the source; d=1 is not covered by this argument.
